title: KGNS honors Gloria Freeman for a decade of volunteering with the Area Health Education Center
excerpt: Gloria Freeman received the October KGNS+ Honors award for 10 years of volunteer work with the Area Health Education Center, KGNS reported.
content:
Gloria Freeman received the October KGNS+ Honors award for 10 years of volunteer work with the Area Health Education Center, KGNS reported, recognizing a decade of behind-the-scenes service to Laredo.

The station presented Freeman with her award during a ceremony held at the KGNS+ building, according to KGNS. Her full story was scheduled to air at 10 p.m. on KGNS News on Oct. 28 and to be available on the station website.

Every month, KGNS recognizes one community member who contributes to Laredo behind the scenes, KGNS reported. Freeman is the October honoree in that series.

A decade of quiet work

The KGNS summary reviewed did not detail Freeman's specific volunteer duties at the Area Health Education Center, and this story does not invent them. What is confirmed is the length of the commitment: 10 years of volunteer work, honored with a named monthly award from the city's television station.

That distinction matters because much of the work that keeps a community healthy and informed is unpaid and largely unseen. Health education centers depend on volunteers to connect residents with information and services, and a decade of steady service is the kind of record that rarely makes headlines on its own.

Freeman's recognition is also a reminder of how local honors work: they do not come with a press release campaign or a large cash prize. They come, in this case, from a local station choosing one person a month and saying, publicly, that the work counted.

What to watch

Residents who want the fuller picture should watch the full KGNS story, which aired Oct. 28 at 10 p.m. and was posted to the station website. That report, not this summary, carries Freeman's own account of why she stayed with the work for 10 years.
